mainTopic: Dough in a kneading bowl, small pieces of חמץ, spoiled food, and the משנה's comparison of חמץ to טומאה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about dough stuck in a kneading bowl. It says dough that patches the bowl is ignored only when it is less than a כזית. The גמרא notes that this clashes with an earlier ברייתא. רב הונא says to delete the lenient one. רב יוסף instead calls it a dispute between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds that leaven set aside as a seat is nullified. אביי shows this does not explain the ruling about less than a כזית, and he places both rulings under רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: dough in the kneading area must be removed, but dough elsewhere, even on the rim, need not be. Two versions are then given of whether רב rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Next, שמואל gives a test for when two half-כזית pieces join, עולא is stricter about pieces in a house, and questions from ארץ ישראל about separate rooms end in תיקו. The גמרא then discusses moldy bread and flour in a tanner's bowl, ruling like רבי נתן. Finally it asks how the משנה can compare the טומאה rule to the חמץ rule. אביי begins an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second ברייתא adds a כזית limit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying dough that reinforces the bowl is ignored only when it is less than a כזית. A full כזית counts as חמץ and as a barrier no matter where it is.
steps.simpleTranslation: …it does not block the immersion, and he does not transgress. Where it is not there to strengthen the bowl, it blocks and he transgresses. When is this said? When it is less than an olive's size. But if it is an olive's size, even in a spot that strengthens the bowl, it blocks and he transgresses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of a second ברייתא, which started on the previous daf, about dough stuck in a kneading bowl. This ברייתא adds a limit based on the size of the dough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough that patches a crack becomes part of the bowl. It is not a חציצה for טבילה, and the owner does not violate בל יראה. This ברייתא says that rule only works for less than a כזית. A full כזית keeps its status as חמץ even inside the bowl.

keyTerms.meaning: Blocks / interposes, so the immersion of the vessel is invalid
Transgresses בל יראה ובל ימצא (owning חמץ on פסח)
Serving to strengthen or patch the bowl
When is this said? (a formula that introduces a limit on the rule)
An olive's volume, the minimum size that matters in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a ברייתא. The words 'it does not block and he does not transgress' refer to dough in a spot that reinforces the bowl, which was mentioned on the previous amud.

phrases.english: it does not interpose, and one does not transgress.
phrases.notes: Refers to dough in a spot that reinforces the bowl.

phrases.english: In a place that does not serve to reinforce —
it interposes and one transgresses.
In what case is this said?
When it is less than an olive-bulk,
but with an olive-bulk —
even in a place that serves to reinforce,
it interposes and one transgresses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second ברייתא, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reinforcing dough is ignored only when it is less than a כזית. A כזית always counts as a barrier and as חמץ.

steps.title: The two ברייתות contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the first ברייתא made no כזית distinction, but the second one does.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contradict each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states that the two ברייתות clash. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא implied that reinforcing dough is nullified even if it is a כזית. The second ברייתא says a כזית is never nullified. Both cannot be right as they stand.

phrases.english: They contradict each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the ברייתא just quoted with the earlier one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of the two ברייתות about בצק שבסדקי עריבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One ברייתא lets a reinforcing כזית be nullified. The other says a כזית is never nullified.

steps.title: רב הונא: delete the lenient ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא resolves the clash by rejecting the lenient ברייתא and keeping the strict one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Remove the lenient one in favor of the strict one.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction by saying the lenient ברייתא is not reliable. We follow the strict one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not try to make the two sources agree. He simply sets aside the lenient one, so a כזית is always חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Remove the lenient one in favor of the stringent one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ברייתא is set aside. The stricter ruling stands.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects to deleting a source. He says each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Have you taken the תנאים out of the world?! It is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a different answer. Both ברייתות are valid, and they simply reflect two opinions among the תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of deleting a text, רב יוסף explains the clash as a real disagreement. He will now need to prove that such a dispute exists.

keyTerms.meaning: Sages of the משנה era; here it means 'a dispute among them'
Did you remove from the world?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Have you removed the tanna'im from the world?!
phrases.notes: He's scolding רב הונא for crossing out part of the text.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's method and offers another answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzMaskana: Both are valid and reflect two tannaitic positions.

steps.title: Proof source: moldy bread must still be destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא rules that moldy, inedible bread must be destroyed, because it can still be used as a leavening agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: Bread that grew moldy must be destroyed, because it can be ground up and used to leaven many other doughs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a ברייתא to show the dispute he mentioned. This first part is the opinion of the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread that is no longer good to eat still counts as חמץ, because it can still leaven other dough. This sets the stage for the next opinion, which limits this rule.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Bread that grew moldy —
one is obligated to destroy it,
because it is fit to be ground up
and to leaven several other doughs with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רב יוסף's claim.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a מחלוקת תנאים about nullifying a כזית of חמץ

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: leaven set aside for sitting is nullified
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר limits the rule to bread kept for eating. A lump of leaven set aside as a seat is nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: When is this said? When it is kept for eating. But a hardened lump of leaven that he set aside to sit on is nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion that disagrees with the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, how the owner treats the חמץ matters. Once he designates it as furniture, it loses its status as חמץ, even if it is large. This matches the first, lenient ברייתא, where dough patching the bowl is nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: A hardened lump of sourdough leaven

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
In what case is this said?
When it is maintained for eating,
but a hardened mass of leaven
that one designated for sitting —
is nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חמץ designated for a non-food use, such as sitting, is nullified.

steps.title: Inference: the תנא קמא holds a כזית is never nullified
steps.stepSummary: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר had to say the lump is nullified, the תנא קמא must disagree. So a כזית stays חמץ even when the owner treats it as useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said 'it is nullified,' it follows that the תנא קמא holds it is not nullified. So he holds: any olive's size, even though one nullifies it, is not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף draws a conclusion from the ברייתא. Its two opinions line up with the two conflicting ברייתות about the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא, who holds a כזית is never nullified, matches the strict ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who allows nullification by designation, matches the lenient ברייתא. So both sources are valid and nothing needs to be deleted.

keyTerms.meaning: The first (anonymous) תנא in the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף: the two ברייתות about dough in the bowl are a מחלוקת תנאים. The strict one follows the תנא קמא (a כזית is never nullified). The lenient one follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (designating it for another use nullifies it).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the גמרא prefers explaining a contradiction as a real dispute over deleting a source. It also sets up the question of whether a כזית of חמץ can lose its status through how it is used.

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בָּטְלָה,
phrases.english: From the fact that Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said it is nullified,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לֹא בָּטְלָה,
phrases.english: it follows that the first tanna holds it is not nullified;
evidently he holds:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל כְּזַיִת, אַף עַל גַּב דִּמְבַטֵּל —
phrases.english: any olive-bulk, even though one nullifies it —
is not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר בָּטְלָה מִכְּלָל דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר לֹא בָּטְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.raayaObject: רב יוסף's claim of a מחלוקת תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied position of the תנא קמא, contrasted with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תנא קמא holds a כזית of חמץ is not nullified by the owner treating it as useless. This matches the strict ברייתא.

steps.title: אביי: Your answer does not cover less than a כזית
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. His answer settles the clash about a full כזית, but not the clash about a piece smaller than a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: You resolved the case of a כזית. Did you resolve the case of less than a כזית?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רב יוסף that his answer is incomplete. It handles the case of a full כזית, but not the case of a piece smaller than a כזית. אביי gives his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the ברייתות follow two different תנאים: the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. That works for a full כזית, because the two do disagree there. But both ברייתות say that even less than a כזית, in a spot that does not reinforce the bowl, is חוצץ ועובר. That clashes with the משנה's rule that less than a כזית is בטל במיעוטו, and splitting the ברייתות between two תנאים does nothing to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive's volume, the minimum amount that counts halachically

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
You resolved the case of an olive-bulk.
phrases.notes: You solved it by saying the ברייתות follow two different תנאים.

phrases.english: Did you resolve the case of less than an olive-bulk?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's answer from Step 4 (backed by the proof in Steps 5-7) as incomplete.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's answer that the two ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תנאים argue only about a full כזית. But the ברייתות also forbid less than a כזית in a non-reinforcing spot, against the משנה's בטל במיעוטו. The dispute between תנאים cannot account for that.

steps.title: Both ברייתות follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: kneading area versus non-kneading area
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives a new answer. Both ברייתות follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The strict one speaks about dough in the kneading area, and the lenient one about dough outside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this ברייתא and that one follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and there is no difficulty. This one speaks about dough in the place where kneading happens. That one speaks about dough not in the place where kneading happens.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops the 'two תנאים' approach. He explains that one תנא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, holds both rulings, each for a different location in the trough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough stuck where kneading happens will mix into the next batch of dough. So it is not nullified, and it must be removed. Dough stuck somewhere that new dough never touches can be nullified. The difference between the ברייתות is where the dough sits, not who said them.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.confusionAlert: אביי does not argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view that useless חמץ can be nullified. He only adds that dough in the kneading area is different, because it will become part of future dough.

phrases.english: Rather, this and that
are both Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
and it is not difficult:
this one is in the place of kneading,
phrases.notes: Strict: the dough must be removed.

phrases.english: that one is not in the place of kneading.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי answers his own challenge with a new way of resolving the ברייתות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different locations of the dough) under a single תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות clash because they follow different תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Dough in the kneading area must be removed, and dough outside it is nullified.

steps.title: רב אשי: Even the rim of the trough counts as outside the kneading area
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that 'not in the kneading area' includes more than the outside back of the trough. It also includes the rim.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Do not say that 'not in the place of kneading' means only the back of the basin. Rather, it also means the edge of the basin.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defines the edges of אביי's lenient case. He makes it wider than we might have assumed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought only the outside of the trough counts as 'not the kneading area.' רב אשי says the rim also counts, because dough being kneaded does not reach it. So dough stuck on the rim can also be nullified.

keyTerms.meaning: The rim / edge of the basin

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Do not say that 'not in the place of kneading' means
only on the back of the basin,
rather, even on the rim of the basin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines a term from אביי's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rim of the trough also counts as 'not the kneading area,' so dough stuck there is nullified.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב אשי needed to say this, since dough plainly does not reach the rim.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether רב אשי's statement teaches anything new. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If kneading never touches the rim, then of course the rim is outside the kneading area. So why did רב אשי bother to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: Isn't it obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 10 was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's statement about the rim
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A statement that teaches nothing new would be pointless.

steps.title: We might have thought dough sometimes drips onto the rim
steps.stepSummary: The answer: without רב אשי, we might have said the rim counts as kneading area because dough sometimes drips there. He teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: sometimes dough drips and reaches there. So he teaches us that it is still not the kneading area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point in רב אשי's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dough does sometimes drip onto the rim, so we might have treated the rim like the kneading area. רב אשי teaches that an occasional drip does not change its status. Dough on the rim stays nullified.

phrases.english: You might have said
that sometimes it drips and reaches there,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge from Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing what we would have wrongly thought without the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because dough sometimes drips onto the rim, the rim counts as kneading area.
steps.terutzMaskana: Occasional dripping does not make the rim part of the kneading area.

steps.title: The halacha follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one version of רב's ruling in the argument between the תנא קמא and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא held that a כזית of חמץ stays חמץ even when the owner treats it as useless. This version of the ruling goes the other way. A lump of leaven that has been set aside for a non-food use, like a seat, is nullified.
steps.whatToRemember: A lump of leaven set aside as a seat (or otherwise made useless) is nullified, following רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (per one version of רב; another version disagrees, Step 16). Dough in a trough's kneading area must be removed, but dough elsewhere, even on the rim, is nullified.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for חמץ that the owner has given a non-food use or that sits in places new dough never touches.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports a ruling on the argument from Steps 5-7 in favor of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version of רב's ruling, the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: leaven set aside for a non-food use, like a seat, is nullified.

steps.title: Challenge from רב's statement about plastering with mortar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ruling that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. It quotes another statement of רב saying a lump of חמץ is nullified only if it is plastered with mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? Didn't רב יצחק בר אשי say in the name of רב: if a person plastered the surface of a lump of leaven with mortar, it is nullified? That means: if he plastered it, yes, it is nullified. If he did not plaster it, no, it is not nullified!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ruling it just quoted (that the הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר). It brings a different statement of רב that seems to point the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר אשי reports that רב requires a real physical act, plastering with טיט, before a lump of חמץ counts as בטל. The גמרא reads this precisely: no plastering means no nullification. That strict requirement does not fit well with saying רב rules like the more lenient רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, so it looks like רב contradicts himself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Is that so?' A formula the גמרא uses to open a challenge
It is nullified, so it no longer counts as חמץ you must destroy
Yes / no. Used here to draw an inference from the exact wording

phrases.english: Is that so?
phrases.notes: This is how the גמרא starts a challenge.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yitzchak bar Ashi say that Rav said:
If one plastered its surface with mortar, it is nullified.
If he plastered it, yes; if he did not plaster it, no!
phrases.notes: The גמרא figures out the opposite case just from how the line is worded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of Step 13 by setting another statement of רב against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's report that רב ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another report of רב requires plastering with mortar before nullification, which implies a stricter position. So רב appears to contradict himself.

steps.title: Different reporters taught different versions of רב
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the scholar who reported one statement in רב's name did not report the other. These are two competing versions of what רב held.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who teaches this statement does not teach that statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. It says the two statements were never meant to stand together, because different students passed down different versions of רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not reconcile the two rulings. It says they reflect a disagreement among the אמוראים about what רב actually said. One tradition has רב ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The other has רב requiring mortar. No one holds both.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who teaches this statement
Does not teach that statement. The two traditions do not go together

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a clever way to make both of רב's statements fit together. The גמרא's answer is simply that they come from two different traditions about רב.

phrases.english: The one who teaches this statement
does not teach that statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּמַתְנֵי הָא לָא מַתְנֵי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Competing traditions (two different reports of the same teacher)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed both statements of רב were reliable together, which created a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statements come from rival traditions about רב's view. Each reporter held only one of them.

steps.title: Second version: the halacha does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: A second version of רב נחמן's report: רב said the הלכה does NOT follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The proof is רב's statement that a lump of חמץ is nullified only when plastered with mortar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a different version: רב נחמן said in the name of רב that the הלכה is not like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. This fits what רב יצחק בר אשי said in the name of רב: if one plastered the surface with mortar, it is nullified, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a second version (איכא דאמרי) of the ruling from Step 13. In this version, the ruling is the opposite: no הלכה like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version there is no contradiction at all. The mortar statement becomes the support for the ruling: since plastering is required, רב is stricter than רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. So the two traditions from Step 15 now line up together inside this version.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה is not like this opinion
Etc. The rest of the quote is understood from earlier

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב's ruling on רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. In the first, the הלכה follows him, and the mortar statement is a separate, competing tradition. In the second, the הלכה does not follow him, and the mortar statement is the proof.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Nachman said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: The halacha is not like Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יִצְחָק בַּר אָשֵׁי אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Yitzchak bar Ashi said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם טָח פָּנֶיהָ בְּטִיט — בָּטְלָה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If one plastered its surface with mortar, it is nullified, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of Step 13's ruling, using the statement from Step 14 as its support.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this version, רב rules against רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and a lump of חמץ is nullified only if it is plastered with mortar.

steps.title: Two half-olive pieces joined by a string of dough
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules on two half-כזית pieces of dough connected by a thin string of dough. If lifting the string lifts both pieces, they count as one כזית and must be removed. If not, there is no obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: if there are two pieces of dough, each half the size of an olive, with a string of dough between them, we check. If picking up the string would lift the pieces along with it, one must destroy them. If not, one does not have to destroy them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from שמואל. It gives a practical test for when small pieces of dough join together to make the size that must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each piece alone is less than a כזית, so on its own it would not need ביעור. The question is whether the thin string connects them into one unit. The test is physical: if lifting the string carries both pieces, they are one connected piece adding up to a כזית, and ביעור is required.

keyTerms.meaning: Half-olive-size pieces, each less than the minimum כזית
A thin string or thread of dough
We look and evaluate the situation
Obligated to remove or destroy the חמץ

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear, hands-on test for when separate small bits of חמץ combine into the amount you must destroy. It is useful for real-life checking for חמץ.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:
Two half-olive-size pieces
with a string of dough between them,
we examine:
whenever, if the string were lifted,
they would be lifted along with it,
one is obligated to remove them.
And if not, one is not obligated to remove them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: שְׁנֵי חֲצָאֵי זֵיתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new related teaching about when small amounts of dough must be removed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two half-כזית pieces joined by a string of dough combine into one כזית that requires ביעור, but only if lifting the string would lift both pieces.

steps.title: עולא limits the leniency to a kneading bowl
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that שמואל's leniency for unconnected half-כזית pieces applies only in a עריבה. In a house, one must remove them.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: We only said this leniency about a kneading bowl. But in a house, a person must get rid of the pieces.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a limit to שמואל's ruling. The 'no need to remove' leniency only applies when the two half-כזית pieces are stuck in a עריבה, not when they are lying around a house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said that two unconnected half-כזית pieces do not have to be removed. עולא narrows this to a עריבה, where each piece stays stuck in place. In a house, the pieces are loose, so the leniency does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when... (a phrase that limits an earlier ruling)

phrases.english: Ulla said:
We only said this in the case of a kneading bowl,
but in a house, one is obligated to remove them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בַּעֲרֵיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of שמואל's leniency from Step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency for unconnected half-כזית pieces applies only in a עריבה. In a house, they must be removed.

steps.title: Why the house is stricter: the pieces may be swept together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains עולא's reasoning: when cleaning a house, a person may gather the pieces and they could land next to each other, forming a full כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because sometimes a person sweeps them up, and they fall next to each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why a house is different from a kneading bowl, and answers right away. While sweeping, the two small pieces can end up together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a עריבה, each piece is stuck in place, so they stay apart. In a house, pieces move around when you clean and can join into a full כזית of חמץ. Because they might combine, they are treated as a real כזית that must be removed.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because sometimes he sweeps them up
and they fall next to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind עולא's distinction in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is a house stricter than a kneading bowl?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a house, the pieces may be swept together and join into a full כזית.
steps.confusionAlert: The two pieces have not actually joined yet. The concern is only that they might join while you clean, and that is enough to require removing them.
steps.whatToRemember: עריבה = pieces stay apart, so no removal is needed. בית = pieces may be swept together, so they must be removed.

steps.title: Questions from the West about pieces in separate areas
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports three questions asked in ארץ ישראל: what if one piece is in a house and the other in an upper story, in a porch, or in an inner room?
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: They asked in the West (ארץ ישראל): A house and an upper story, what is the law? A house and a porch, what is the law? Two rooms, one inside the other, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא brings questions that build on his own rule about a house. If the two pieces are in different parts of a home, could they still be swept together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The house rule depends on the fear that the pieces will be swept together. Each case tests how far apart the pieces can be for that fear to still apply. An upper story, a porch, and an inner room are each separate areas, so the pieces may be less likely to meet.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked in the West (ארץ ישראל)
Porch or portico, an open covered area
One inside the other (an inner room off an outer room)

phrases.english: Ulla said: They asked in the West (Eretz Yisrael),
a house and an upper story, what is the law?
A house and a porch, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי בָתִּים זֶה לִפְנִים מִזֶּה מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Two rooms, one inside the other, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the house rule from Steps 18-19 to cases where the pieces are in separate areas.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the fear of sweeping the pieces together apply when they are in separate areas of a home?

steps.title: The questions remain unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the questions of the West stand without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion without answering the three questions. It says תיקו, which means 'let it stand.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source or reasoning was found that settles whether separate areas of a home count as one place for this rule. The questions are left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions of Step 20 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether half-כזית pieces in separate areas of a home must be removed stays an open question (תיקו).
steps.whatToRemember: תיקו means the גמרא could not decide. The three cases (upper story, porch, inner room) stay unresolved.

steps.title: Moldy bread still counts as food
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that bread too moldy for people, but still edible for a dog, can become impure as food (with a כביצה). It may also be burned together with impure תרומה on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: bread that became moldy, so people won't eat it but a dog still can, can become impure as food if it is the size of an egg. It may also be burned together with impure bread on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about bread that spoiled for people but not for dogs. The first opinion says it still counts as food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test for 'food' here is whether a dog would still eat it, not whether a person would. So the bread can still receive טומאת אוכלין. Because no person will eat it anymore, we no longer need to protect pure תרומה bread of this kind from becoming impure, so it may be burned together with impure תרומה on פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity that food can receive
The size of an egg, the minimum amount for food to become impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two measurements. A כזית (olive size) matters for the ביעור of חמץ. A כביצה (egg size) is the amount needed for food to become impure.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Bread that became moldy
and became unfit for a person to eat,
but a dog can still eat it —
it becomes impure with food impurity, if it is an egg-size,
and it may be burned together with impure (תרומה) on פסח.
phrases.notes: No one will eat it, so there is no need to keep it pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the unanswered questions of the West (תיקו).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bread unfit for people but fit for a dog is still food for טומאה, and pure תרומה of this kind may be burned with impure תרומה on פסח.

steps.title: רבי נתן says the moldy bread cannot become impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן disagrees. Once the bread is unfit for people, it can no longer become impure as food.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי נתן they said: it does not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא brings a second opinion. רבי נתן says this moldy bread no longer counts as food at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, the test is human food. Once people won't eat it, it loses its status as food, even if a dog would still eat it.

phrases.english: In the name of Rabbi Natan they said:
It does not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food unfit for humans loses its food status for טומאה.

steps.title: Which opinion does the משנה in טהרות follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: food meant for people stays impure until even a dog won't eat it. It asks whose view this משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what we learned in a משנה: 'They stated a rule about purity: anything meant as human food stays impure until it becomes unfit even for a dog to eat'? Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה and asks which side of the argument it agrees with. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the dog test: food keeps its status until even a dog won't eat it. That is the same test the תנא קמא used, so the גמרא wants to match the משנה to the right opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Purity laws (the order of the משנה dealing with them)

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow, that we learned in a משנה:
They stated a rule about purity:
Anything meant as human food —
stays impure until it becomes unfit
even for a dog to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the argument in the ברייתא to a משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion in the ברייתא the משנה in טהרות follows.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה does not follow רבי נתן. It matches the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view? Not רבי נתן's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the משנה goes against רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן says food stops being food as soon as people won't eat it. The משנה says it stays food until even a dog won't eat it. So the משנה must follow the תנא קמא.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two tests for when spoiled food stops counting as food. The תנא קמא and the משנה in טהרות say: when a dog won't eat it. רבי נתן says: as soon as a person won't eat it.

phrases.english: Whose view? Not in line with Rabbi Natan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the תנא קמא, not רבי נתן.

steps.title: Flour in a tanner's bowl before פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: if flour was put in a tanner's bowl within three days before פסח, one must remove it. If it was put in earlier than that, there is no obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a tanner's bowl that someone put flour into. If it was within three days before פסח, he must remove it. If it was more than three days before, he does not have to remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about flour used in making leather. It tells us when that flour still counts as חמץ that must be removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bowl's bad smell spoils the flour, but this takes about three days. If the flour has been there for three days before פסח, it is already spoiled and not food. If less time has passed, it is still edible חמץ and must be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: A tanner's bowl, used in making leather

steps.confusionAlert: 'Within three days' means the flour was put in less than three days before פסח, so it has not yet had time to spoil.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A tanners' bowl
into which one put flour,
within three days (before פסח) — he must remove it.
Earlier than three days,
he is not obligated to remove it.
phrases.notes: By then it is already spoiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case of spoiled food, also involving רבי נתן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Flour in a tanner's bowl counts as spoiled after three days. If it was put in within three days of פסח, it must be removed.

steps.title: רבי נתן: once hides are in, no removal needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the three-day rule applies only when no hides were put in. If hides were put in, the flour is spoiled at once and need not be removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן said: when does this apply? When no hides were put into the bowl. But if hides were put in, even within three days he does not have to remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן limits the ברייתא's three-day rule to a bowl without hides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foul hides spoil the flour right away, so there is no need to wait three days. This fits רבי נתן's general view: once people won't eat something, it stops being food.

keyTerms.meaning: When does this apply? (introduces a limit on a rule)

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan said:
When does this apply?
When he did not put hides into it,
but if he put hides into it —
even within three days
he is not obligated to remove it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי נָתָן: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ברייתא's three-day rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once hides are in the bowl, the flour is spoiled right away and need not be removed.

steps.title: רבא rules like רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like רבי נתן. Once hides are in, even one day or one hour is enough to spoil the flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows רבי נתן, even if it was only one day, or even one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final ruling: we follow רבי נתן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no waiting period once hides are added. Even one hour in the bowl makes the flour spoiled, so it is not חמץ that must be removed.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice, flour in a tanner's bowl with hides in it is not חמץ that must be removed, even after only an hour.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical halacha: flour spoiled by foul hides is no longer edible at all, so it loses its status as חמץ that must be removed. This differs from merely moldy bread (Step 5), which must still be destroyed because it can leaven other dough.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Natan,
even after one day
and even after one hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the halacha on רבי נתן's addition.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once hides are in the bowl, the flour is spoiled immediately and there is no obligation to remove it.

steps.title: The משנה's line about impurity and blocking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: for טומאה, dough the owner minds is a חציצה (blocks the טבילה), but dough he wants to stay counts as part of the bowl.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly regarding impurity: if he minds the dough, it blocks. If he wants it to stay, it is like the bowl itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about dough stuck in a kneading bowl, now regarding טומאה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a bowl is dipped in a מקוה, nothing may block the water from reaching it. If the owner minds the dough and plans to remove it, the dough is a separate thing that blocks. If he wants it to stay, it becomes part of the bowl and does not block.

keyTerms.meaning: Minds it, is bothered by it and wants it removed
Blocks, an interposition between the item and the מקוה water
Wants it to stay in place

phrases.english: And similarly, regarding impurity,
phrases.notes: Referring to dipping the bowl in a מקוה to purify it.

phrases.english: if he minds it, it blocks;
and if he wants it to stay,
it is like the kneading bowl itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי נתן and the tanner's bowl, the גמרא returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For טבילה, whether dough blocks depends on whether the owner minds it.

steps.title: How can size and minding be compared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'similarly': the חמץ rule depends on size, while the טומאה rule depends on whether the owner minds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really alike? There, the matter depends on size. Here, the matter depends on minding!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the משנה's word 'similarly,' because the two rules seem to work in completely different ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חמץ, the משנה said a כזית in one place must be removed, and less than that is nullified. So size decides. For טבילה, size does not matter at all; only the owner's attitude decides. So how can the משנה call them 'similar'?

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (a challenge to a comparison)
A set measure or size (here, a כזית)

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There (חמץ), the matter depends on the size.
phrases.notes: A כזית in one place must be removed.

phrases.english: Here (טומאה), the matter depends on minding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word 'וכן' in the משנה line just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's word 'וכן' (similarly), which links the חמץ rule to the טומאה rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two rules use different tests. One goes by size and the other goes by the owner's attitude, so calling them 'similar' does not fit.

steps.title: רב יהודה rereads the משנה as a contrast
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers by changing the reading: the משנה should say 'for טומאה it is NOT so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Say that the משנה reads, 'And regarding impurity it is not so.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה solves the problem by changing the משנה's words from 'similarly' to 'it is not so.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה is contrasting the cases instead of comparing them, the difficulty disappears. חמץ goes by size, but טבילה does not. For טבילה, minding decides, exactly as the rest of the line says.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way): a textual correction

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: Say (read it as):
"And regarding impurity, it is not so."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation: changing the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה compares טומאה to חמץ, so both should go by the same test.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה contrasts them. Only חמץ goes by size, and טומאה goes by minding.

steps.title: אביי objects that the משנה says 'similarly'
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יהודה's change, because the משנה clearly says 'similarly.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But the משנה teaches 'And similarly regarding impurity'!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יהודה: you cannot turn 'similarly' into its opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing 'וכן' (similarly) into 'אינו כן' (not so) flips the meaning of the משנה completely. Such a big change is too much just to solve a difficulty. So the comparison must be explained as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But it teaches! (pointing to the actual wording)

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But it teaches "And similarly regarding impurity"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָא וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יהודה's answer from step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's change of the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה plainly says 'similarly.' Reversing it into 'not so' is too drastic a change to accept.

steps.title: אביי begins his own explanation
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to explain how the משנה can keep the word 'similarly.' His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: This is what it means: 'And similarly…'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens his own answer, which keeps the משנה's wording. This line only sets up his explanation; the details come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'הכי קאמר' signals that אביי will not change the words. He will explain what the משנה really means by them. He will show how the טומאה case can truly be 'similar' to the חמץ case.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: rejecting the earlier approach and offering a new one
This is what it means (an explanation, not a change of text)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse 'הכי קאמר' with 'אימא.' רב יהודה's 'אימא' changed the words. אביי's 'הכי קאמר' keeps the words and only explains them.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
This is what it is saying: "And similarly…"
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud.
